summary: TechCrunch's weekly transportation newsletter The Station covers a turbulent week for GM's Cruise, which lost its California driverless permits and then paused driverless operations in all its markets. It also rounds up deals (Flexport/Convoy, Ola Electric, Pony.ai/Neom, Stellantis/Leapmotor), EV investment pullbacks at Ford and GM-Honda, the UAW strike reaching tentative deals with Ford and Stellantis, and other mobility news.
one_line: The Station newsletter recaps Cruise pausing all driverless operations after California permit suspension, plus EV pullbacks, major funding deals and UAW strike progress.
key_facts: The California DMV suspended Cruise's driverless and deployment permits, with the California Public Utilities Commission following shortly after, ending robotaxi operations in San Francisco just months after Cruise received its last needed permit.

Two days later Cruise paused driverless operations in every market where it charged for robotaxi service, including Austin, Houston and Phoenix; it had also quietly launched a few driverless vehicles in Miami.
At an all-hands meeting the day after the DMV suspension, CEO Kyle Vogt told staff Cruise had not paused operations elsewhere and was re-evaluating how it discloses information to regulators.
Gogoro showed at the Japan Mobility Show 2023 that its scooter batteries can power Project X, a three-seater minicar concept from the Foxconn-led Mobility in Harmony Consortium (MIH).
MIH aims to sell 100,000 Project X minicars per year in India, Thailand and Japan starting in 2025, with a price around $20,000 and support for autonomous driving Levels 2 to 4.

Flexport is in talks to acquire the technology of shuttered digital freight startup Convoy, per WSJ; Flexport founder Ryan Petersen recently retook the CEO role and laid off about 20% of staff, around 600 people.
Ola Electric raised $384.4 million (about $240 million in debt) led by Temasek, valuing it at about $5.4 billion; Pony.ai received $100 million from Neom.

Stellantis made a €1.5 billion ($1.59 billion) deal for a 20% stake in Zhejiang Leapmotor Technologies, forming Leapmotor International, a 51%/49% Stellantis-led joint venture for sales and manufacturing outside China.
Ford is delaying about $12 billion in planned EV investments, including a second battery plant with SK On, due to softening demand for premium EVs.
General Motors and Honda ended plans to build millions of affordable, smaller electric vehicles amid high interest rates, battery costs and softer EV demand.
Waymo vehicles are now available through the Uber app, starting in Phoenix, five months after the companies announced their multi-year agreement.

The UAW reached tentative deals with Ford and Stellantis in the strike's sixth week, but called a surprise walkout at GM's Spring Hill, Tennessee plant, where 4,000 workers assemble engines and three Cadillac models.
Nio opened its 2,000th Power Swap Station in China, aiming for 2,300 by the end of 2023; Nikola was awarded $165 million from founder Trevor Milton in arbitration.
